shots.purpose: Open on a mysterious brass machine and establish the multiply-by-ten motif.
shots.action: A glowing number tile and brass lever wake the machine.

shots.purpose: Introduce Mira, Ari and the three place-value chambers.
shots.action: Mira reveals the hundreds, tens and ones chambers to Ari.

dialogue.speaker: mira
dialogue.text: Inside this machine, every digit has a place.

shots.purpose: Represent twenty-three as two tens and three ones.
shots.action: Tiles two and three settle into the tens and ones chambers.

dialogue.speaker: mira
dialogue.text: Here is twenty-three: two tens and three ones.

shots.purpose: Show multiplication by ten as a one-place-left shift.
shots.action: Both digits travel one chamber left and a zero occupies the ones chamber.

dialogue.speaker: mira
dialogue.text: Multiply by ten, and every digit moves one place left.

shots.purpose: Explain that the trailing zero is an occupied empty ones place, not decoration.
shots.action: A labeled zero tile locks the empty ones chamber after the shift.

dialogue.speaker: ari
dialogue.text: The zero holds the empty ones place.

shots.purpose: Ask the learner to apply the rule without leaking the answer.
shots.action: Forty-seven waits in the tens and ones chambers while the learner thinks.

dialogue.speaker: mira
dialogue.text: Your turn. What is forty-seven times ten?

shots.purpose: Reveal and verify the learner answer only after thinking time.
shots.action: The digits shift left, zero fills ones, and the full equation resolves.

shots.purpose: Close on the reusable conceptual rule.
shots.action: Mira and Ari celebrate beside the locked place-value machine.

dialogue.speaker: mira
dialogue.text: Times ten means every digit shifts one place left.

overlays.source: ×10: every digit shifts one place left
